literal: Like a balance rod that, having made itself level, weighs the weight, remaining without bending to one side is the ornament of the noble.
translation: To remain unbiased without leaning to any one side, just like a balance scale that first levels itself and then weighs justly, is the true ornament of the wise.
modern: முதலில் தன்னைச் சமமாக ஆக்கிக்கொண்டு, பின் பொருள்களின் எடையை அளவிடும் தராசுக்கோல் போல, நடுவுநிலைமையோடு அமைந்து ஒரு பக்கமும் சாயாமல் இருப்பதே சான்றோர்களுக்கு அழகாகும்.
explanation: This couplet uses the beautiful metaphor of a balance scale to define the virtue of impartiality. A scale must first be perfectly level before it can accurately weigh objects. Similarly, a noble person must first establish an unbiased mind and then judge matters without leaning to any one side. This steadfast fairness, free from prejudice, is described as their finest ornament.
